cuts.item: athletic trainer model replaced by EMT model for required sports (full-time athletic director kept)
athletic trainer position (savings net, about 46,000 / 40 grand)
outsourcing of school custodians / facilities and grounds

statements.statement: Corrected FY27 deficit after removing a double-counted $500,000 free cash and about $19,000 in trim costs; currently anticipated at this figure (caption truncated).
The $500,000 in free cash had been double counted in the earlier deficit figure.
The original budget deficit number reported was 2.4 million, now down to 1.9.
High school principal and assistant principal salary line was overbudgeted, saving this amount in the updated projection.
Goal is to get the restoration-budget override ask under 2 million; currently at a million nine.
The 1.9 million restoration ask keeps the school share at about 57% of the budget; the town manager would like 53.
A member said the committee is being told it has to cut $900,000 from the budget.
Debus busing cost information shows a 15% increase.
Returning to the original athletic structure (half-time AD, full-time trainer) would add this amount to the budget.

warnings.prediction: The cuts budget would be bad based on prior experience; the chair called it the 'shoot your favorite puppy budget'.
Athletic trainer and athletic director will be on the table in a cuts budget.
If there are cuts, athletics will be decimated because it was first in line and had the fewest cuts last year.
Without an override, a lot of things being discussed won't be possible; the schools would be down a million or 2 million.

warnings.condition: if the override ask is cut back toward 53%
warnings.prediction: Would have to eliminate the whole restoration budget and still need an override just for level service.
Cutting the athletic trainer would lose support from sports parents for the override.

warnings.condition: if the ask goes higher than 53%
warnings.prediction: Other committees might support a bifurcated or tiered override if the ask goes above 53%.
Outsourcing custodians would cost more in the long run; savings short-term at best.
This is a make-or-break year; nothing left to trim.
